treatments.name: Metformin
treatments.summary: Metformin, together with lifestyle modification, is the background therapy to which ACP adds newer agents when glycemic control is inadequate.

evidence.quote: ACP recommends adding a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor or glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) agonist to metformin and lifestyle modifications
evidence.statement: Newer agents are recommended as additions to existing metformin and lifestyle therapy, which positions metformin as the background first-line drug.

treatments.name: Lifestyle modification
treatments.summary: Lifestyle modification is part of the baseline regimen that newer drugs are added to.

evidence.quote: to metformin and lifestyle modifications in adults with type 2 diabetes and inadequate glycemic control
evidence.statement: Lifestyle modification is assumed as part of baseline therapy alongside metformin.

treatments.name: SGLT-2 inhibitors
treatments.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and inadequate glycemic control on metformin and lifestyle modification
treatments.summary: Strongly recommended as an add-on to metformin to reduce mortality, cardiovascular events, CKD progression and heart-failure hospitalisation.

evidence.quote: ACP recommends adding a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor or glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) agonist to metformin and lifestyle modifications in adults with type 2 diabetes and inadequate glycemic control (strong recommendation; high-certainty evidence).
evidence.statement: ACP strongly recommends adding an SGLT-2 inhibitor or a GLP-1 agonist to metformin when glycemic control is inadequate.

evidence.quote: Use an SGLT-2 inhibitor to reduce the risk for all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events, progression of chronic kidney disease, and hospitalization due to congestive heart failure.
evidence.statement: SGLT-2 inhibitors are preferred when the goal is to reduce mortality, cardiovascular events, CKD progression or heart-failure hospitalisation.

treatments.name: GLP-1 agonists
treatments.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and inadequate glycemic control on metformin and lifestyle modification
treatments.summary: Strongly recommended as an add-on to metformin to reduce mortality, cardiovascular events and stroke.

evidence.quote: ACP recommends adding a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor or glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) agonist to metformin and lifestyle modifications in adults with type 2 diabetes and inadequate glycemic control (strong recommendation; high-certainty evidence).
evidence.statement: ACP strongly recommends adding an SGLT-2 inhibitor or a GLP-1 agonist to metformin when glycemic control is inadequate.

evidence.quote: Use a GLP-1 agonist to reduce the risk for all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events, and stroke.
evidence.statement: GLP-1 agonists are preferred when the goal is to reduce mortality, cardiovascular events or stroke.

treatments.name: DPP-4 inhibitors
treatments.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and inadequate glycemic control on metformin and lifestyle modification
treatments.summary: ACP recommends against adding a DPP-4 inhibitor to metformin to reduce morbidity and all-cause mortality.

evidence.quote: ACP recommends against adding a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor to metformin and lifestyle modifications in adults with type 2 diabetes and inadequate glycemic control to reduce morbidity and all-cause mortality (strong recommendation; high-certainty evidence).
evidence.statement: ACP strongly recommends against DPP-4 inhibitors as the add-on to metformin.
